beats.say: Almost eight hundred years ago, a pope's letter accused people of worshipping a black cat.
So I shrank to mouse size, to follow this cat through history.
Pope Gregory the Ninth sent it in twelve thirty-three.
It warned of a secret devil cult, spreading across Germany.
The stories came from a hunter of heretics, named Conrad of Marburg.
Historians now think Conrad and a few others made the cult up.
A teacher in Paris even claimed the name Cathar, for one group of heretics, came from the Latin word for cat.
Another story said the devil showed up as a white cat, as big as a dog, covered in bird feathers.
Not everyone feared cats. In ancient Egypt, the goddess Bastet had a cat's head.
In her temple city, Bubastis, thousands of cat mummies have been found.
And the black fur? One tiny change in one gene.
The strangest part? It says a black cat, as big as a dog, walked backwards down a statue.
And then every member of the cult kissed its rear end.
So if a black cat crossed your path, would you keep walking?
Eight hundred years later, black cats are still paying for one very weird letter.
Follow me. Next, a giant bird that stands still like a statue, then claps its beak like a drum.
